title: Diary of the Late Rajah of Kolhapoor, during His Visit to Europe in 1870
short_title: Diary of the Rajah of Kolhapoor
summary: Rajaram, Rajah of Kolhapoor (1850–1870), ruler of a princely state in western India, sailed for Europe in 1870 with Captain Edward West, his guardian, his Parsee tutor, and eleven attendants. He kept this diary in English, in short daily entries, from his arrival in Paris on 12 June to 16 November: months in and around London, with visits to Windsor, Parliament, schools, factories, and theatres; the British Association at Liverpool; Scotland; Dublin; and the journey home through Belgium, Germany, and the Tyrol. He died at Florence on 30 November 1870 and was cremated there. West’s introduction gives the history of Kolhapoor and of the Rajah’s education. A postscript, appendices of official papers (durbars, the cremation, memorial meetings, the adoption of a successor), and a supplement reprinting Lady Verney’s article from Good Words complete the book.
